principles: Single writer choke-point: all host-run capture reuses the existing dispatch-usage seam; no second ledger writer path
Diagnostics-only: usage rows never gate workflow (gateEvidence=false semantics preserved)
Provider truth over estimates: provider-reported counts come only from real host output; absence is recorded as source=unavailable, never fabricated or zeroed
Fail-closed caps before spawn: budget and concurrency refusals happen pre-spawn and are recorded as blocked rows
Read-only retro attribution: the sweep never mutates transcript stores and never backfills the ledger
drivers: Burn evidence 2026-07-10: host-side runs are invisible to the ledger - 368.9M cumulative input in one 30-hour desktop thread, ~16M input per minute from five parallel codex exec reviewers
B-d8ef canonical launcher specs are the mechanical contract every lattice-initiated host run must already follow - the natural single choke point

Verified host surfaces: agy exposes no per-call usage; canonical codex launcher is --ephemeral (no rollout) but exec --json emits a terminal turn.completed usage event; claude stream-json result usage is parseable today via parseClaudeCliOutput

options.name: host_run choke-point command reusing the dispatch-usage seam
pros: Preserves the single-writer completeness guarantee from the usage-ledger execution plan
Canonical launcher argv enforced mechanically at one place
storyId/agentType/phase/reviewRunId bound at call time, not reconstructed later
Budget and concurrency caps (T2) enforceable pre-spawn with blocked ledger rows
cons: Adoption requires guidance updates so operators stop launching raw codex exec / claude --print

options.name: Extend dispatch_run and dispatch records to cover reviewer and quorum runs
cons: Dispatch records and policy semantics are dispatch-scoped; overloading them for reviewer/quorum runs muddies process facts and forces synthetic dispatch records
Reviewer/quorum context (reviewRunId, lane) does not fit the dispatch record shape

options.name: Sweep-only: skip launcher capture and attribute everything post-hoc from transcript stores
cons: Attribution stays an estimate forever; no call-time binding of storyId/phase
Violates the completeness-by-construction principle; caps unenforceable

chosen: host_run choke-point command reusing the dispatch-usage seam
rationale: Only the choke-point command preserves the single-writer completeness guarantee while making attribution call-time-bound and making the T2 budget/concurrency caps enforceable before spawn; the sweep remains a clearly-labeled estimate layer for sessions lattice did not launch.

preMortem.scenario: Operators keep launching raw codex exec so the choke point is bypassed and the ledger stays sparse
preMortem.trigger: Guidance, reviewer templates, or muscle memory still show raw host commands
preMortem.consequence: M1 ships but coverage does not improve; burns stay invisible
preMortem.mitigation: CHK-004 rewrites every reviewer/quorum/autopilot guidance surface to name the choke-point command; the M2 sweep doubles as a bypass detector because foreign exec sessions in lattice cwds show up in the report

preMortem.scenario: A host CLI upgrade changes the turn.completed or stream-json result shape and the parser silently stops finding usage
preMortem.consequence: Usage rows degrade to unavailable without anyone noticing, silently under-counting
preMortem.mitigation: Absence is recorded as explicit source=unavailable rows with a reason; smoke fixtures pin the parsed shapes; the usage report surfaces unavailable counts so drift is visible

preMortem.scenario: The concurrency cap deadlocks or blocks legitimate quorum work
preMortem.trigger: Stale slot entries left by a crashed or killed host run
preMortem.consequence: Reviews stall behind a fail-closed cap
preMortem.mitigation: Slot registry uses pid liveness plus mtime staleness detection with automatic reclaim; refusal messages print the exact live-run list and the env override

preMortem.scenario: The sweep double-counts split claude assistant events or misreads cumulative codex totals as per-turn values
preMortem.trigger: Transcript quirks: one assistant message emitted as multiple JSONL events sharing message.id; codex total_token_usage is cumulative
preMortem.consequence: Attribution report overstates burns and misleads cost decisions
preMortem.mitigation: Dedupe claude usage by message.id/requestId keeping the last value; treat codex totals as cumulative last-value per session; fixtures encode both quirks; report is labeled non-authoritative

preMortem.scenario: Ledger writes slow down or break long reviewer runs
preMortem.trigger: Corrupt ledger file or fs error during a 30-minute reviewer run
preMortem.mitigation: The seam never throws (existing contract); host output passthrough is independent of ledger writes; the host exit code propagates unchanged
